newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-HODGSON LEAVES INTER FOR BLACKBURN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HODGSON LEAVES INTER FOR BLACKBURN.

text.p: Internazionale Milan said on Wednesday that English coach Roy Hodgson would leave at the end of the season to become manager of Blackburn Rovers.
The news, announced first by the English premier league club, initially appeared to take Inter by surprise but the club later confirmed Hodgson was moving.
"It was not a bolt out of the sky for me," club chairman Massimo Moratti said.
"Hodgson had told me a few days ago. What surprises me more is the speed with which the news came out of England, but the English have got us used to these things."

The announcement came just three months after Hodgson extended his contract with Inter until June 1999 following a 3-0 defeat of Juventus in the domestic cup and a conclusive 5-1 win against Portugal's Boavista in the UEFA Cup.
Moratti said the separation was amicable and by mutual agreement.
"Hodgson conducted the matter with his usual intelligence and correctness, and it is in that spirit of freedom that I let him go despite the contract to 1999," he said.

Rovers' chairman Robert Coar said Hodgson, who has been at Inter for 16 months, was expected to take over from caretaker boss Tony Parkes at Ewood Park in July although he would be welcomed earlier if the Italian club agreed.
"We are delighted that Roy Hodgson has agreed to join us and to have secured the services of a man with great knowledge of the European football scene," Coar said in a statement.
"This confirms our intention to be a leading club in both the premier league and Europe."
In a statement issued on November 20, Inter said Hodgson had turned down an approach from Blackburn and had extended his contract, originally due to end in June this year, for a further two years.
Hodgson was in Naples with his squad preparing for an Italian Cup semifinal second leg match against Napoli on Wednesday night.

English premier league side Blackburn were left to find a new manager after Swede Sven-Goran Eriksson changed his mind about coming to Ewood Park from Sampdoria last week and decided to stay in Italy.
Eriksson has not said officially yet where he will be coaching next season but most of the signs point to Lazio, who fired Czech coach Zdenek Zeman earlier in the year.
However, Inter could also now become an option.
Moratti said he had no successor lined up to take over from Hodgson yet.

Hodgson, 49, has not worked as a manager in his native England since he left Bristol City in 1982. He made his name in Europe, enjoying success with the Swiss national team which qualified for the 1994 World Cup finals against the odds.

Great things were expected of his hugely expensive Inter side, which includes a host of foreign talent including French international Youri Djorkaeff and England's Paul Ince, but the team has fired irregularly this season.
Fans had recently heckled him and Moratti said the experience had left a mark. "He's a man who suffers if he does not succeed, if he fails to have the 100 percent backing of public opinion."
Inter are third in the league, seven points adrift of leaders Juventus, and Hodgson has been criticised by the local media for failing to come up with a winning strategy.

Although the club are favourites to win the domestic cup and are also still in the UEFA Cup, their title aspirations have taken a big knock. Ironically, it was Eriksson's Sampdoria, who beat them 4-3 at home, that did much of the damage.
